research_text:
# Research brief: `javax.crypto.spec.IvParameterSpec` and the CrySL rule `IvParameterSpecSpec`

**Main limitation.** I could not retrieve the text of `IvParameterSpec.crysl` from the URL you gave. My tools were web search only, with no direct fetch, and no search result contained that file. Question 4 therefore cannot be answered from the source itself, and I have not quoted any clause. The rule description in your input is not verbatim rule text. I treated it as unverified.

## Q1. What the API governs, and what the finding refers to

- **What the API governs.**
  - The class is an `AlgorithmParameterSpec` that holds an initialization vector (IV).
  - Oracle gives CBC mode as an example. Source: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/IvParameterSpec.html
  - It has two constructors, `IvParameterSpec(byte[] iv)` and `IvParameterSpec(byte[] iv, int offset, int len)`, plus `getIV()`.
  - The three-argument form uses bytes `iv[offset]` through `iv[offset+len-1]` as the IV.
  - The Javadoc says the array contents are copied to protect against later modification.
- **What the finding refers to.**
  - The detector message is "unknown". The reported violation type is `UnsatisfiedConstraint`.
  - No official Java documentation defines either term, so I cannot say which API event or value the finding refers to.
  - The only available evidence is the CrySL literature, which says the `IvParameterSpec` rule requires a `randomized` predicate on the IV byte array. Sources:
    - https://eclipse.dev/cognicrypt/documentation/crysl/
    - https://www.bodden.de/pubs/tse19CrySL.pdf
  - That is consistent with your input (`randomized[iv]` required, `preparedIV[this]` ensured), but it does not establish the specific finding.
  - The papers say that when CogniCrypt SAST cannot ensure a predicate for an `IvParameterSpec` use, the missing predicate carries forward to later objects such as the cipher.

## Q2. Documented correct and safe usage, and recommended remediation

- **Argument validity.** Per the Java SE 21 Javadoc (URL above):
  - The one-argument constructor throws `NullPointerException` if `iv` is null.
  - The three-argument constructor throws `IllegalArgumentException` if `iv` is null or `iv.length - offset < len`.
  - The three-argument constructor also throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` for out-of-range `offset` or `len`.
  - The Java SE 25 page words the last case as negative `offset` or `len`: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/IvParameterSpec.html
  - I found no documented minimum for `len`, such as `len > 0`. The `len > 0` and `offset >= 0` conditions in your input appear to come from the CrySL rule, not from the Javadoc.
- **Where the IV comes from.**
  - The Javadoc for `IvParameterSpec` gives no randomness or uniqueness guidance.
  - The older JCA Reference Guide says the IV should be random but does not need to be secret: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/6/docs/technotes/guides/security/crypto/CryptoSpec.html
  - The current JCA guide says the same parameters used for encryption must be used for decryption: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/security/java-cryptography-architecture-jca-reference-guide.html
  - The JCA sample code says that if you give no IV when initializing a cipher for encryption, the implementation generates a random one. You then retrieve it with `Cipher.getParameters()`.
  - The `Cipher` Javadoc says `getIV()` is useful when a random IV was created: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/Cipher.html
  - For GCM, the `Cipher` and JCA documentation says to use a different IV value each time the same key is reused for encryption: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/technotes/guides/security/crypto/CryptoSpec.html
- **Remediation.** The official sources give no remediation text for a "non-randomized IV" finding. Any such guidance would come from the CrySL rule set, not from Oracle.
- **Decryption.**
  - The JCA guide's requirement to reuse the same parameters is the official basis for supplying a stored IV when decrypting.
  - An arXiv paper (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.07808) reports that CogniCrypt SAST wrongly flagged static IVs during decryption. It says the CrySL rule set was changed in response.
  - The current `Cipher.crysl` requires `preparedIV[paramSpec]` only when `encmode == 1`, for the CTR, CTS, CFB and OFB modes: https://github.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/blob/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/Cipher.crysl
  - I could not check whether `IvParameterSpec.crysl` has any decryption-specific condition of its own.

## Q3. Compatibility

- **Persisted and wire formats.**
  - The Javadoc says nothing about serialization or encoding of `IvParameterSpec`. It documents `getIV()` and copy-on-construction only.
  - The JCA guide says the decrypting side must receive the encryption parameters. It describes `SealedObject` as attaching those parameters to the sealed content.
  - So changing how an IV is produced does not change the class's own format. Any stored or transmitted layout belongs to the application.
- **Platform versions.**
  - `IvParameterSpec` has existed since Java 1.4: https://www2.cs.duke.edu/csed/java/jdk1.4.2/docs/api/javax/crypto/spec/IvParameterSpec.html
  - Android lists it from API level 1: https://developer.android.com/reference/javax/crypto/spec/IvParameterSpec
  - The Javadoc for the three-argument constructor has changed across versions, in the exception documentation and the copy note. I found no behavioral deprecation.
  - The JDK-8267068 review thread on the mail-archive shows the `@throws` documentation was being corrected, for example the `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` wording: https://www.mail-archive.com/security-dev@openjdk.org/msg13152.html
- **Migration path.** I found no official migration guidance specific to this class. Mode-specific points are documented elsewhere. For example, GCM uses `GCMParameterSpec`, and GCM IVs must not be reused with the same key.

## Q4. The exact CrySL rule

- **Verbatim matching clause.** Not retrievable, so none is quoted. Nothing below is quoted from the rule file.
- **What I could verify from secondary documentation:**
  - A CrySL rule's `SPEC` clause names the one fully qualified class the rule governs. The EVENTS section lists method and constructor calls of that class. Sources:
    - https://eclipse.dev/cognicrypt/documentation/crysl/
    - https://d-nb.info/127168148X/34 (a University of Stuttgart thesis)
  - The ECOOP paper says `IvParameterSpec` has a rule containing only constructor calls: https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol109-ecoop2018/LIPIcs.ECOOP.2018.10/LIPIcs.ECOOP.2018.10.pdf
  - The thesis notes a generated rule contained only one of the original method calls, which suggests the rule has been revised over time.
- **Unresolved, because I could not read the file:**
  - the exact event declarations and their parameter lists
  - whether `offset` and `len` are bound in `c1`
  - the exact constraint text
  - whether a same-named method on a different type can match. Based on the documented `SPEC` semantics, matching appears to be tied to the governed class, but I could not confirm this from the rule.

## Remaining open questions

- What `UnsatisfiedConstraint` with the message "unknown" means in the reporting tool.
- The verbatim text of `IvParameterSpec.crysl` at the cited commit or branch. The URL points to `master`, which can change.
- Whether the rule applies any decryption or IV-provenance exemption.
